title: Organic cotton in Maharashtra
body: In 1995 an NGO suggested that cotton, the biggest user of chemical pesticides, could be grown organically. A senior cotton scientist doubted the idea and asked whether India wanted to 'go naked'. Later, about 130 farmers committed 1,200 hectares of land to grow cotton organically according to the standards of the International Federation of Organic Agriculture Movement. The produce was tested by a German accredited agency, AGRECO, and was found to be of high quality. The NGO's founder pointed out that about 78 per cent of Indian farmers are marginal farmers owning less than 0.8 hectare, and argued that for such farmers organic agriculture is more profitable in terms of money and soil conservation in the long run.
